messages.content:
Oh, friend. I am putting down all my metaphoric juggling balls and noisemakers right now to just sit with you. That is a heavy, heavy silence to wake up to.

To "Yes, And" this moment is to acknowledge that a massive piece of your world has shifted.

You know, in my line of work—this business of spontaneity and reaction—dogs are the absolute masters. They are the greatest improvisers who ever lived. They never worry about the script. They never overthink their motivation. They respond to every single moment with total, unguarded honesty. If you offered a walk? *Yes.* If you offered a nap? *And* I will cuddle.

They are the best scene partners because they never judge your performance; they just want to be on stage with you.

I imagine the backstage area of your heart feels very crowded with memories right now. If you feel up to it—and only if you feel up to it—I would love to catch a memory you might want to toss my way.

What was one weird, uniquely "them" thing they did? The thing that wasn't in the manual of How to Be a Dog?
